summary: Dedicated: Org admin cannot update autoscaling policy after RBAC v2 enforcement (403 from console)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer on Dedicated cannot change autoscaling policy from Console (Dedicated capacity settings). Action fails with 403 immediately after RBAC v2 enforcement rollout.

Impact
- Customer cannot adjust min/max replicas / scale-up thresholds for their dedicated GPU pool.
- Blocks their planned traffic increase and on-call runbook requires being able to tune autoscaling quickly.

Customer / Org context
- Apex Cyber Insurance (Dedicated, enterprise procurement in progress). They use separation-of-duties: Billing Admin is separate from Org Admin; customer expects a dedicated/ops admin role can manage autoscaling without full org admin privileges.

Environment
- Prod, us-east
- Console action path: Dedicated → Capacity → Autoscaling Policy → Save

Steps to reproduce
1) Login as customer admin user (role reported as “Org Admin” in their org).
2) Navigate to Dedicated capacity autoscaling settings.
3) Modify any field (e.g., max_replicas) and click Save.

Expected result
- Autoscaling policy updates successfully; audit log entry includes actor, role, decision.

Actual result
- 403 Forbidden in Console.
- Console toast: “You don’t have permission to perform this action.”

Observed errors / logs (from customer HAR + Redwood request ID)
- HTTP 403 from control plane endpoint: PUT /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/autoscaling-policy
- x-redwood-request-id: req_01HPC9S8J9Y7W8K4QF2V0Z9M3A
- Error body (sanitized): {"error":"forbidden","reason_code":"AUTHZ_DENIED_MISSING_PERMISSION","required_permission":"dedicated.autoscaling_policy.write"}

Initial notes
- Timing lines up with RBAC v2 enforcement being enabled on Dedicated admin endpoints.
- Likely mismatch between default role permission bundle and the permission required by the endpoint (or role mapping regression for existing org admins).

Support asks
- Confirm which role(s) should be able to update dedicated autoscaling policies.
- Provide short-term workaround that doesn’t require granting broad Org Admin if possible.
- Provide ETA for fix and confirm audit logging of authz decision context.
comments:
2025-02-19 09:14 PT — Rachel Kim (Reporter, CS)
Customer reports: “We were able to change autoscaling last week. As of today, Save fails with a permission error.” They attached a HAR and screenshot. Impact: they need to raise max replicas ahead of an internal load test.

Request ID provided: req_01HPC9S8J9Y7W8K4QF2V0Z9M3A

2025-02-19 09:36 PT — Owen Phillips (Assignee, Support Escalation)
Confirmed on our side: request returns 403 with reason_code AUTHZ_DENIED_MISSING_PERMISSION and required_permission dedicated.autoscaling_policy.write.

I checked recent changes: Dedicated capacity admin endpoints were newly guarded under RBAC v2 (see PR sources/github/redwood/pr_18505.json). Suspect policy bundle missing allow rule for Org Admin or the endpoint is using a new permission string not included in v0.1 bundle.

Looping in Platform Authz / Control Plane for confirmation + fix plan.

2025-02-19 10:02 PT — Owen Phillips
Workaround proposal (pending customer confirmation): temporarily grant the affected user the “Org Admin” role (if they are not already) OR add a second user with Org Admin for capacity operations.

Customer states the user is already “Org Admin” per Console, which suggests either: (a) role assignment display mismatch vs evaluated roles, or (b) Org Admin policy missing dedicated.autoscaling_policy.write.

Next step: ask customer to export their role assignments (screenshot is fine) and confirm user email + org slug.

2025-02-19 11:11 PT — Customer (via Rachel Kim)
Confirmed user is Org Admin. Org slug: apex-ci-prod. User: admin.ops@apex-ci.example.
They cannot use Billing Admin due to SoD policy and would prefer a narrower role than Org Admin long-term, but they need immediate unblocking.

2025-02-19 11:40 PT — Owen Phillips
Pulled authz decision logs for req_01HPC9S8J9Y7W8K4QF2V0Z9M3A. Actor role_ids evaluated did not include the expected Org Admin role; only “Developer” was present.

Hypothesis: role cache is stale or role assignment change not invalidating policy cache for this org (seen in a separate thread recently). Asking Platform to confirm cache invalidation behavior for role assignment updates.

Immediate workaround for customer: reassign role to force invalidation (remove + re-add Org Admin) or have them log out/in to refresh session claims. I’ll coordinate with CS to do this safely.

2025-02-19 12:05 PT — Rachel Kim
Customer removed and re-added Org Admin role for admin.ops@apex-ci.example and logged out/in. They can now Save autoscaling policy successfully.

They still want a clear guidance on which least-privileged role should be used for ongoing operations (autoscaling changes).

2025-02-20 09:18 PT — Owen Phillips
Eng update: root cause confirmed as cache invalidation gap—role assignment changes were not reliably invalidating org-scoped policy cache across all control plane nodes, causing stale role_ids in evaluation and false 403s.

Eng is preparing a fix PR to improve invalidation + add metrics/alerts for stale role evaluation (cache hit rate vs role version). For tracking, Control Plane points to policy cache/invalidation work (see sources/github/redwood/pr_18477.json as related) and the Dedicated endpoint guard PR (sources/github/redwood/pr_18505.json).

Customer-facing guidance: if a user’s role was recently changed and they see unexpected 403, reassign role + re-login as a short-term mitigation until fix is deployed.

2025-02-22 14:27 PT — Owen Phillips
Fix merged + rollout started. Change includes:
- Force invalidation on role assignment updates (org_id keyed) and background refresh on authz middleware.
- Add structured log field role_assignment_version and export to authz decision logs.
- Dashboard alert for “shadow-deny after role change” spikes.

Customer validation requested: please retry autoscaling policy updates without role toggle if possible.

2025-02-23 10:10 PT — Rachel Kim
Customer confirmed issue no longer reproduces. They changed autoscaling policy twice today without any role reassignment.

They requested follow-up on least-privileged access model for Dedicated ops (separate from billing/security). I pointed them to our role definitions overview and noted that custom roles are planned post-GA; for now, use Org Admin for capacity operations or a dedicated ops admin user under Org Admin with tight internal controls.

Closing ticket.
resolution: Resolved via cache invalidation fix for RBAC v2 role assignment updates (stale role_ids causing false denies). Short-term workaround was to remove/re-add Org Admin role and re-login to refresh evaluation context. Fix deployed and customer confirmed autoscaling policy updates succeed consistently.
customer_visible_next_steps: Recommended creating a dedicated operations admin user with Org Admin for Dedicated capacity operations until custom roles are available; provided guidance on diagnosing unexpected 403s using reason_code and request_id for Support.
internal_follow_ups: Add runbook note for Support: role-toggle + re-login workaround for suspected stale role cache until fully eliminated.
Ensure policy bundle includes clear mapping for Dedicated capacity operations permissions in role matrix documentation.
Consider default “Dedicated Ops Admin” role proposal for separation-of-duties (product follow-up).
